paper.title: AudioMarathon: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Long-Context Audio Understanding and Efficiency in Audio LLMs

evidence.section: Abstract; benchmark construction (10 subsets across speech content, audio scene, and voice characteristics)
evidence.paraphrase: 6,567 questions over 90-300 s audio (2,250-7,500 audio tokens) spanning speech, sound, and music; tasks require multi-hop inference over long-range temporal dependencies, so the model must hold and re-access evidence distributed across the whole clip.

The benchmark systematically evaluates KV-cache eviction policies (Random, KNorm, TOVA, SnapKV) and audio-token pruning policies (Random, FastV, DART, and the authors' time-aligned Frame pruning) at 30%/60%/90% compression, i.e. it measures how well different retention/eviction policies over the audio KV store preserve task accuracy.

adjudication_notes: Retained as memory_adjacent, not a core memory benchmark: the benchmark targets long-context audio understanding and inference efficiency, and there is no explicit evaluation of a persistent cross-session or streaming agent memory. It is included because its efficiency track directly evaluates KV-cache eviction and audio-token retention policies, which are inference-time memory-management policies over a non-text (audio) modality.
No architecture record created: the paper proposes no new memory architecture (the only novel component is the 'Frame' time-aligned pruning baseline used as an evaluation condition).

Scope confirmed against ten existing memory_adjacent records, in particular lvomnibench.json which is likewise recorded as memory_adjacent for evaluating long-horizon comprehension rather than memory architecture.
